# G-11 -- the triage list of the real-tree secret scan (see docs/security-probes/G-11.md).
#
# One line per secret-class finding that the scanner (scripts/oss_audit/) reports on the tracked
# tree and that a human has reviewed and accepted:
#
#   <rule>\t<path>\t<count>
#
# The rule ids are the ones of scripts/oss_audit/rules.py. The count is the number of
# occurrences the finding had when it was reviewed. A finding that is not listed here, or a
# listed finding that occurs more often than it did when it was reviewed, fails the probe: the
# tree then holds a secret the team has not triaged.
#
# The list carries no secret material -- a rule id, a path and a count. The scanner's own output
# (its masked hints) stays out of the repository, as scripts/oss_audit/README.md requires.
#
# S01-S12 (the credential-shaped rules) are triaged over the whole tracked tree. S13 (a
# password-like assignment) is triaged outside test/ and handoffs/: those two directories hold
# fixture values and agent run logs by design, and their findings are not gated.
#
# What each entry is (the probe does not judge a finding, it only judges that the finding was
# triaged):
#
#   S10 handoffs/WF03-ISS07*  a bearer token quoted in the task description of a run of the old
#                              agent pipeline (2026-09). The SAME 64-character value is in 12
#                              tracked files: 3 carry the "Bearer " context (these are the S10
#                              rows below) and 9 carry it as a queue_auth_token assignment
#                              (handoffs/WF02-REQ390/393/395/396 and handoffs/WF03-ISS0761/
#                              0774/0788), which the S13 rule matches but which is not gated
#                              under handoffs/ by design. Reviewed: the runs are over and the
#                              token is not a live credential of the platform. The owner decides
#                              whether it is rotated; until it is, treat it as live (the
#                              scanner's README says so). The probe does not touch run logs.
#   S11 ...                   the bare JWT of the UAT preflight fixtures (a signed token with a
#                              fake signature, used to test a request without a role).
#   S13 config/, docs/, priv/, scripts/
#                              the environment-variable reads of config/runtime.exs, the YAML
#                              documents and the Keycloak realm templates: the matcher reads a
#                              key name and the value that follows it, not a credential.
#
# Reviewed on 2026-11-23 (tree eb5b98d4d, origin/main ad80271e9 merged into the G-11 branch; the
# gated findings are unchanged from the review of 2026-11-22). Regenerate with the command in
# docs/security-probes/G-11.md and account for every changed line in the review.
